title: refactor(dm): classify Bloc errors via Reportable matrix (#4590)
body:
## Description

Classification sweep over `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/**` per the [Reportable decision matrix](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#decision-matrix). Two generic catches that mixed recoverable + invariant paths are now narrowed: `ArgumentError` / `FormatException` stay raw (matrix-NO, recoverable) and any remaining throw is `Reportable`-wrapped (matrix-YES, invariant). All other DM-area catches stay raw with 2-line classification comments matching the precedent at `other_profile_bloc.dart:165` and `my_profile_bloc.dart:183`.

**Outcome: 2 new YES sites + 13 NO classifications.** YES identifiers lift into a new `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/reportable_sites.dart` per the spec's 2+ sites rule. The existing `_onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` Reportable (from #4402) moves to use the same constants class.

### Classification table

| File:Line | Method | Catch sees | Matrix row | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `conversation_bloc.dart:89` | `_onStarted` (stream onError) | Drift / rxdart stream IO | Network/IO | NO |
| `conversation_bloc.dart:104` (narrowed) | `_onMessageDeleted` `on Object` + `is ArgumentError` | `ArgumentError` (msg gone / not ours) | API/domain | **NO** (recoverable branch) |
| `conversation_bloc.dart:104` (narrowed) | `_onMessageDeleted` generic catch | `StateError('Failed to sign kind 5 …')` and any other non-`ArgumentError` throw | Invariant | **YES** (new) → `ConversationBlocReportableSites.onMessageDeleted` |
| `conversation_bloc.dart:179` | `_onMessageSent` | Explicit `throw Exception(result.error)` (domain), repo IO. Narrowing here would need a typed exception for the domain throw — out of scope (separate PR). | API/domain | NO |
| `conversation_bloc.dart:232` | `_onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` | Narrowed: `on Object` + `is ArgumentError` skip; rest is invariant | Invariant | **YES (existing, #4402)** → lifted to `ConversationBlocReportableSites.onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` |
| `message_request_actions_cubit.dart:39,52,65` | `decline` / `markAllRead` / `removeAll` | Drift writes | Network/IO | NO |
| `request_preview_cubit.dart:87` | `load` | Drift reads | Network/IO | NO |
| `conversation_list_bloc.dart:102` | `_onStarted` (stream onError) | Drift + follow-stream IO | Network/IO | NO |
| `conversation_mute_cubit.dart:75` | `toggleMute` | `SharedPreferences.setString` IO | Network/IO | NO |
| `conversation_mute_cubit.dart:100` (narrowed) | `_load` `on FormatException` | Corrupted prefs JSON | API/domain | **NO** (recoverable branch) |
| `conversation_mute_cubit.dart:100` (narrowed) | `_load` generic catch | `cast<String>()` lazy `TypeError` — stored shape is wrong | Invariant | **YES** (new) → inline `context: '_load'` (single-site, stays inline per spec) |
| `conversation_actions_cubit.dart:66,85,97,112` | `report` / `block` / `unblock` / `remove` | API/repo calls | Network/IO | NO |
| `dm_unread_count_cubit.dart:23` | constructor stream `onError: addError` tear-off | Drift stream IO | Network/IO | NO |

### New file

- `mobile/lib/blocs/dm/reportable_sites.dart` — `ConversationBlocReportableSites` with `onSelfWrapRecoveryRequested` and `onMessageDeleted` constants. Conversation-mute's single new YES site stays inline (`context: '_load'`) per the spec's single-site rule.

### New tests

- `conversation_bloc_test.dart` — `ConversationMessageDeleted`: asserts `StateError` is wrapped in `Reportable<StateError>` while `ArgumentError` continues to flow raw.
- `conversation_mute_cubit_test.dart` — `_load`: asserts `cast<String>()` `TypeError` is wrapped in `Reportable<TypeError>` via a capturing `BlocObserver` (addError fires during construction).

**Related Issue:** Closes #4590

## Out of Scope

- **Narrow `_onMessageSent` (line 179)** by introducing a typed `_DmSendDomainFailure` to replace the bare `throw Exception(result.error)`. The dominant case is a domain throw that floods under flaky relays — wrapping that in Reportable without filtering would be matrix-incorrect. Defer to a follow-up.
- **Sibling area sweeps** (notifications #4591, welcome/publish #4592, video-editor #4594) are independent child issues under epic #4336.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` on all 10 changed files — Formatted 10 files (0 changed)
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — No issues found
- `flutter test test/blocs/dm/` — 160 tests pass (+2 new)
- `flutter test packages/dm_repository` — 240 tests pass

## Test plan

- [x] All existing DM bloc tests pass without modification (runtime types into `addError` preserved on the recoverable branches)
- [x] New `Reportable<StateError>` test for `_onMessageDeleted` YES path
- [x] New `Reportable<TypeError>` test for `_load` YES path
- [x] Analyzer + format clean
- [ ] CI green (Analyze + Tests + Format + Generated Files)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [x] 📝 Documentation

title: fix(search): drop idle placeholder on Explore → Search with prefilled query
body:
## Summary

Tapping into Explore's search bar and typing 2+ characters auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` after a 300ms debounce. The destination then flashed **"Enter a search query / Discover something interesting"** for another ~300–600ms before BLoCs were dispatched and section skeletons appeared. On slow networks the window stretched, reading as a flash, error, or hang. This PR makes the destination drop the idle placeholder when a route arg query is pending, and dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously on AppBar mount so the BLoCs advance from `initial` this same frame.

Closes #3802. Companion to parent epic #3801.

## Root cause

`SearchResultsView` keyed the idle short-circuit on `VideoSearchBloc.state.status == initial` alone. That signal correctly identifies "no query entered" (the load-bearing PR #3199 fix for #3023's infinite skeleton) but does NOT distinguish it from "query just arrived as a route arg, AppBar dispatch is still pending its 300ms UI debounce."

## Changes

- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_view.dart` — add optional `String initialQuery = ''`. Gate the idle short-circuit on `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so it matches the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. Falls through to sections (whose own skeletons render on `initial || loading/searching` with empty results) when a searchable query is pending. Inline comment cites PR #3199 / #3023 so a future reader doesn't simplify the conditional back to the buggy form.
- `lib/screens/search_results/view/search_results_page.dart` — pass `initialQuery` from `_SearchResultsBody` to `SearchResultsView` (1 line).
- `lib/screens/search_results/widgets/search_results_app_bar.dart` — reorder `initState` so the controller text is seeded BEFORE the listener is attached. When `initialQuery.isNotEmpty`, dispatch `*QueryChanged` events synchronously to all four BLoCs. The BLoCs' `debounceRestartable` still applies; same-query dedup guards coalesce any late-arriving event. Focus model intentionally untouched — that's sibling issue #3020 / #3803 territory.

All 5 entry points to `SearchResultsPage` go through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: query)` (Explore auto-push, `@mention` link tap, universal link, deep link, GoRoute), so this fix applies uniformly.

### Commit history

1. `1f99c2b6` — initial fix.
2. `2407333d` — self-review follow-up: tighten the view's idle gate from `isEmpty` to `trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` so reachable edge cases (whitespace-only or 1-char deep links like `/search-results/a` and `/search-results/%20%20`) don't render infinite skeletons (a #3023-class regression in the corner). Two extra regression tests pin the corrected behavior.

## Scope clarification

Per the issue body: "Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical." This PR is scoped to the intermediate-state symptom only. The focus and keyboard work belongs to:

- #3020 — keyboard collapses (assigned to @untreu2)
- #3803 — canonical focus behavior (assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz)

The parent epic #3801 calls for these three children to land as one cohesive transition PR (Gate 2). I scoped this PR to #3802 alone; bundling is the epic driver's call.

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/screens/search_results/` → **85 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/{video,user,hashtag,list}_search test/blocs/search_results_filter` → **119 passing**
- [x] `flutter test test/screens/explore_screen_pure_test.dart` → 12 passing
- [x] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → no issues
- [x] `dart format` → clean

New test coverage:
- `search_results_view_test.dart` — new `with non-empty initialQuery` group asserts `SearchSectionInitialState` does NOT render when `initialQuery` is non-empty + status is initial, and that the all-filter section list renders instead. Plus two regression tests pinning the whitespace-only and sub-min-length cases to the idle placeholder (cures the #3023-class edge case).
- `search_results_app_bar_test.dart` — adds missing `_MockListSearchBloc` mock (the existing setUp had a gap), plus three new tests: synchronous dispatch on non-empty `initialQuery`, NO dispatch on empty `initialQuery`, and no double-dispatch after the 300ms debounce window elapses.
- Existing idle-state tests preserved verbatim — PR #3199's load-bearing behavior is unchanged for the empty-query path.

## Manual device testing guide

### What changed (one-paragraph context for QA)

When you typed 2+ characters in Explore's search bar and the app auto-pushed to `/search-results/:query`, you saw a brief "Enter a search query / Discover something interesting" placeholder for ~300–600ms before search results loaded — especially noticeable on slow networks. After this fix, the destination shows section skeletons immediately and lands on real results once they arrive. The empty-query case (opening the search screen directly) still shows the "Enter a search query" placeholder as before.

### Build

Pick one:

- **Preview web build** (fastest, no local setup): open the `Mobile PR Preview` link from this PR's checks. The bot posts a `https://<hash>.openvine-app.pages.dev` URL on every push.
- **Local install** on the device:
  ```bash
  git fetch origin
  git checkout fix/3802-search-intermediate-state
  cd mobile
  flutter pub get
  flutter run --release   # release matters — debug mode is slower and masks the symptom
  ```
- **TestFlight / internal build** if one is cut later — pull the build tagged with this PR's SHA.

Notes:
- The bug is more visible in `release` than `debug` (debug is slow anyway, so any flash is harder to attribute).
- The bug is most visible on slow networks. Throttle to "Slow 3G" via iOS Settings → Developer → Network Link Conditioner (or Android Developer Options → Networking → Network type → "GPRS"), or use a proxy throttle.

### Golden path — primary repro from issue #3802

1. Launch the app. Sign in if needed.
2. Tap the **Explore** bottom-nav tab.
3. Tap the search bar at the top of Explore.
4. Type `hello` (or any 2+ character query). **Stop typing** and wait.
5. After ~300ms the app navigates to the search results screen.

What to look for (frame-by-frame):

| Frame | Before this fix (broken) | After this fix (correct) |
|---|---|---|
| Navigation completes | Screen renders with a centered search icon + **"Enter a search query"** + **"Discover something interesting"** | Screen renders with shimmer **skeletons** for People / Lists / Tags / Videos sections |
| ~300–600ms later | Skeletons appear (the placeholder fades) | (same skeletons continue, no flash transition) |
| Results arrive | Real results render | Real results render |

- **Pass criteria**: at no point during the transition does the "Enter a search query" copy appear.
- **Fail signal**: if you see "Enter a search query" or "Discover something interesting" even briefly, the fix didn't apply.

Tip: if you can't catch it visually, screen-record at 60 fps and step through frames.

### Slow-network case — the issue's "feels like a hang" complaint

Same steps as Golden path, but throttle to Slow 3G first.

- **Pass**: skeletons hold for as long as the network needs, then results land. No misleading "Enter a query" text. No fallback to an error state until/unless results genuinely fail.
- **Fail**: the "Enter a search query" copy appears, OR the screen looks empty/blank for any period.

### Direct entry to /search-results (regression check for #3023 — DO NOT skip)

This is the load-bearing case from PR #3199. **This must still work the OLD way.**

Two ways to trigger:

A. Universal/deep link with empty query — open the app from a `divine.video/search-results/` link (no query) if you can construct one, OR

B. In the running app: Explore → tap search bar → land on `/search-results/` with no query in the field.

- **Pass**: centered "Enter a search query" / "Discover something interesting" placeholder renders. **This is correct** — it was the #3023 fix.
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely (that's #3023 reopening).

### Edge cases — sub-min-length & whitespace-only query (the F1 finding addressed in commit 2)

Reachable via deep / universal links — try if you can construct them, otherwise skip:

1. Open `divine.video/search-results/a` (single character) — or build a URL pointing at `/search-results/a` and open it from another app.
2. Open `divine.video/search-results/%20%20%20` (whitespace-only, URL-encoded).

- **Pass for both**: idle placeholder "Enter a search query" renders. (BLoCs gate on `length >= 2` so sub-min queries never reach the network; the view correctly treats them as idle.)
- **Fail**: shimmer skeletons render indefinitely.

### Other entry paths — same expected behavior

These all converge through `SearchResultsPage(initialQuery: ...)` so they should all behave consistently:

1. Tap an `@username` mention in a comment (links via `linkified_text`) — should land on search with the username pre-filled, **no misleading placeholder**.
2. Open the app from a universal link `https://divine.video/search-results/<query>` — same.
3. Open from a push-notification deep link with a search term — same.

- **Pass**: skeletons + results. No "Enter a search query" flash.

### Focus / keyboard — explicitly NOT in scope here

This fix does NOT change focus or keyboard behavior. Those are tracked separately in:
- **#3020** (keyboard collapses when typing in Explore → search page) — assigned to @untreu2
- **#3803** (canonical focus model) — assigned to @NotThatKindOfDrLiz

For #3802 QA: **don't flag** keyboard or focus issues against this PR. The destination field will not auto-focus when navigated with a pre-filled query — that's the existing behavior and intentionally untouched.

### Filters & deep search — confirm nothing else regressed

1. Land on `/search-results/hello` (golden path).
2. Tap the **filter pill** (top-right). Switch between All / People / Videos / Tags / Lists.

- **Pass**: each filter renders its skeletons → results. No "Enter a search query" appears on any filter tab even before results arrive.
- **Fail**: any filter renders the empty-query placeholder.

### Empty results — make sure we don't show idle instead of empty

1. Search a query with truly no results (e.g. random keyboard mash like `xqzqzqzq`).
2. Wait for results to settle (~1–5 seconds).

- **Pass**: each section shows its appropriate empty-state ("No results found for X" / "Try a different search term"). **Not** "Enter a search query."
- **Fail**: the idle placeholder shows after BLoCs have completed.

### Error/timeout (people search) — confirm degraded-empty UI

Same as above on a flaky network. If NIP-50 user search times out:

- **Pass**: People section shows the retry affordance (per the #3791 / #3804 fix that already landed). Other sections show their results or empty states.
- **Fail**: idle placeholder shows instead of the retry UI.

### Sign-off checklist

```
[ ] Golden path: type `hello` in Explore, no "Enter a search query" flash
[ ] Slow-3G repro: same, with throttle on
[ ] Direct-entry (empty query): "Enter a search query" placeholder DOES render
[ ] Sub-min-length deep link `/search-results/a`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] Whitespace-only deep link `/search-results/%20%20`: idle placeholder renders
[ ] @mention tap → search: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Universal link with query: skeletons not placeholder
[ ] Filter switch: each filter shows skeletons until results, never placeholder
[ ] Empty result (mash query): empty-state not placeholder
[ ] People-timeout: retry UI not placeholder
[ ] Devices: iOS + Android, recent + min-supported OS
```

If any row fails, file a comment on this PR with the device, OS, network condition, and a screen recording.

## Notes for reviewers

- The doc comment over the `isIdle` conditional in `search_results_view.dart` is intentional — `tests-guard-intentional-workarounds` precedent. Don't simplify it back to `isInitialStatus` alone or #3023 reopens.
- The idle gate uses `initialQuery.trim().length < minSearchQueryLength` rather than `isEmpty` so it mirrors the BLoC handlers' own gate exactly. The looser `isEmpty` form regressed reachable edge cases in commit 1; commit 2 tightened it.
- Parent epic #3801 Gate 1 (auto-push vs explicit submit) is owned by Product / Design and unresolved. This fix is safe under either outcome: if Gate 1 keeps auto-push, the misleading state is fixed; if Gate 1 removes auto-push from Explore, the universal-link / deep-link / `@mention`-link entry paths still benefit from this fix.

title: search: avoid misleading intermediate state during Explore → Search transition
body:
## Summary

The Explore → Search transition currently shows a brief intermediate full-screen state before meaningful search results are available. On slower connections this can feel like an error, flash, or hang rather than an intentional transition.

Parent epic: #3801

## Agent Brief

This issue is about the **intermediate visual state** during Explore → Search navigation.

Confirmed:
- Explore auto-pushes `/search-results/:query` on partial input.
- The search results screen becomes visible immediately.
- Real search work and useful results arrive later.
- Users can interpret the transient screen as broken or hung.

Do not collapse this issue into keyboard/focus behavior. They are related, but not identical.

## Confirmed facts

From reproduction logs:
- Explore route is active.
- App pushes `/search-results/:query` immediately after partial input.
- Search screen becomes visible in 2–3ms.
- Search results and timeout fallback occur meaningfully later.

From code:
- Explore pushes to `SearchResultsPage.pathForQuery(query)` from a debounced text listener.
- Search results view can render an idle/initial placeholder before async search state catches up.

## Problem

Users are seeing a route transition before the UI has a stable, intentional search state to present. The result is a visible intermediate screen that reads as a flash, error, or hang.

## Questions to resolve

- Should the route transition be delayed until search state is ready?
- Should Explore retain control until explicit submit?
- If the route transition stays, what exact loading/placeholder state should be shown?
- How should slow-network or timeout fallback be communicated?

## Acceptance criteria

- The Explore → Search transition no longer presents a misleading or broken-looking intermediate state.
- Slow-network behavior is intentional and visibly understandable.
- The visual state between “typing” and “results available” is explicitly defined.
- Tests cover the chosen transition behavior.



---

## Assignee
`@realmeylisdev`

## Weekly Priority
`P1`

## Sequencing
- Start after entry behavior is agreed.
- Can run alongside focus continuity work.

## Parent
- `#3801`

## Dependencies
- Start after the subgroup agrees the entry behavior.

## Agent Execution Notes
Agents working from this issue must:
- treat this child issue as the execution source of truth for intermediate-state cleanup
- read `#3801` before implementation

## Engineering Standard
Fix the problem without adding new technical debt. If the touched path already has known audit or refactor debt, repay the relevant portion as part of the implementation instead of layering on a narrow patch.

title: feat(keycast): mid-session token refresh on 401 and app resume
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4588

Keycast OAuth tokens expire after ~3 hours. Users who leave the app backgrounded (common with iOS background modes for push notifications) return to a stale token and all RPC-backed operations (reporting, signing, encryption) fail silently — this was the root cause behind reporting surfaces failing (#4586).

Two recovery paths:

- **On app resume (Option A):** `AuthService.onAppResumed()` now checks if the stored OAuth session has expired and proactively refreshes it before any RPC call is attempted.
- **On 401 response (Option B):** `KeycastRpc._call()` detects 401 responses and invokes a `TokenRefreshCallback` to obtain a fresh access token, then retries the request once. This catches tokens that expire mid-session without an intervening app backgrounding.

Both paths share the same refresh mechanism via `OAuthClient.refreshSession()`.

### Changes

**`keycast_flutter` package:**
- Added `TokenRefreshCallback` typedef
- `KeycastRpc` constructor accepts optional `onTokenRefresh` callback
- `KeycastRpc.fromSession()` factory forwards `onTokenRefresh`
- `_call()` detects 401, invokes callback, updates token, retries once
- Extracted `_sendRequest()` to avoid duplication between initial call and retry

**`auth_service.dart`:**
- Added `_refreshAccessToken()` — the callback wired into every `KeycastRpc` instance
- Added `_refreshOAuthTokenOnResume()` — proactive refresh on app resume when session is expired
- Wired `onTokenRefresh: _refreshAccessToken` at all three `KeycastRpc.fromSession()` construction sites (init, background upgrade, signInWithDivineOAuth)

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new tests for 401 retry behavior in `rpc_client_test.dart`
- [x] All 178 `keycast_flutter` package tests pass
- [x] Analyzer clean on both changed files
- [ ] Manual: sign in with Divine OAuth, wait for token expiry (~3 hours or force-expire in staging), trigger a report/sign operation → should succeed transparently
- [ ] Manual: background app past token expiry, resume → RPC operations should work without re-login

title: refactor(state): define and enforce Riverpod/BLoC migration boundaries
body:
## Description

Defines and enforces the Riverpod/BLoC ownership boundary that was missing from the codebase. Previously, docs said BLoC/Cubit is the default for UI state but provided no concrete allowed/disallowed patterns, no bridge inventory, no enforcement mechanism, and no canonical example to copy from.

**Related Issue:** Closes #3339

---

### What changed

**Documentation**

- `docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md` — replaced stale PR evidence (#1908 closed, #1894/#1903 merged with dates); added Ownership Boundary section; added 7-row Allowed/Disallowed patterns table with `ValueKey` guard code example; added Canonical Template Screens table; added Current Bridge Inventory table with removal criteria for all four `*BridgeProvider`s; tracked to #3339
- `docs/STATE_MANAGEMENT.md` — added Quick Reference section with the one-sentence rule, canonical examples table, and copy-paste Page/View pattern
- `.claude/rules/state_management.md` — mirrored Allowed/Disallowed table and template screen references for agent-written code

**Template screen (Page/View split)**

- `mobile/lib/screens/video_engagement/video_engagement_list_view.dart` *(new)* — `VideoEngagementListView` extracted as a public `StatelessWidget` with zero Riverpod dependency
- `mobile/lib/screens/video_engagement/video_engagement_list_screen.dart` — ABOUTME updated to call out the canonical bridge pattern and reference the PRD; delegates to `VideoEngagementListView`

**Bridge TODO comments**

- `mobile/lib/router/app_shell.dart` — replaced vague comments on the four `*BridgeProvider` watches with `// TODO(#3339):` comments stating each bridge's purpose and concrete removal criterion

**CI enforcement**

- `mobile/scripts/check_riverpod_boundary.sh` *(new)* — fails CI if `@riverpod` or `StateProvider(` appears outside `providers/` or `services/` directories; prints violating files and links to the PRD; currently zero violations
- `.github/workflows/mobile_ci.yaml` — new step in the `generated-files` job wiring the guard into CI

**Tests**

- `mobile/test/screens/video_engagement/video_engagement_list_screen_test.dart` *(new)* — 8 widget tests: Page renders View, loading state, success with pubkeys, empty state, likers/reposters titles, initial event dispatch, and a dedicated `VideoEngagementListView` isolation test that renders the View without any `ProviderScope`

---

### Why VideoEngagementListScreen as the template

197 lines, already had a `StatelessWidget` inner view, uses `ref.watch` with a record `ValueKey` guard (the auth-flip-safe pattern). Zero logic changes — purely structural extraction and documentation. The three canonical examples now cover all common bridge variants:

| Screen | Pattern |

| `AppsDirectoryScreen` | `ref.read` stable service, no `ValueKey` needed |
| `VideoEngagementListScreen` | `ref.watch` auth-sensitive repos + record `ValueKey` guard |

---

### Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|-----------|--------|

  Please look at the following checklist to ensure that your PR can be accepted quickly:

## Description
The retryCount stored in Hive was never incremented between retry cycles. _performUploadWithRetry read retryCount from the persisted PendingUpload, then wrote it back unchanged (retryCount: currentRetry instead of retryCount: currentRetry + 1). Every iteration therefore read 0, logged "Upload attempt 1/6", and wrote 0 back — the counter was frozen and the status never transitioned from uploading to retrying.

- retryCount increments after each failed attempt (1 → 2 over a fail-then-succeed cycle)

title: chore(main): log and classify startup-step failures (#3588, #4336)
body:
Tracking child of epic #4336. PR K in the epic plan — addresses 6 empty `catch (_) {}` blocks in `mobile/lib/main.dart` startup paths that hide cold-start failures.

## Problem

Re-audit of `mobile/lib/main.dart` against `origin/main` (2026-05-20) found **6 empty catch blocks** in startup-coordinator paths:

| Line | Context |
|-----:|---------|
| 868 | startup-coordinator phase |
| 895 | startup-coordinator phase |
| 915 | startup-coordinator phase |
| 926 | startup-coordinator phase |
| 1169 | (mid-startup) |
| 2120 | (late startup / shutdown) |

These were not in the original audit (#3588 cited ~12 sites across providers/packages but missed `main.dart`).

A failure in any of these silently suppresses, so a cold-start regression that breaks one initialization step is invisible until the dependent feature also breaks downstream — a much harder bug to triage.

## Scope

For each of the 6 sites, choose one of three:

1. **Safe-to-fail step** (e.g., optional cache warming): keep the catch, add a one-line comment explaining the no-op contract per [`.claude/rules/error_handling.md` "Document No-Operations"](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#document-no-operations).
2. **Recoverable step** (e.g., optional Firebase init on unsupported platforms): add `Log.warning('startup step X failed', error: e, stackTrace: st)` so the failure is visible in the unified log + bug-report capture.
3. **Must-not-fail-silently step** (e.g., FCM token registration): forward through `CrashReportingService.instance.recordError(e, st, reason: 'main_startup_step_<name>')` with the `ReportableError` decision deferred to PR A2 / #3758.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 6 empty `catch (_) {}` blocks at lines 868, 895, 915, 926, 1169, 2120 either logged or annotated with a contract comment.
- [ ] PR description includes a `(line, step name, classification (no-op / warning / recordError), reason)` table.
- [ ] No new silent-failure patterns introduced.
- [ ] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` green.

## Relationship to #3588

This is a sibling of #3588 (not a replacement). #3588's original scope (12 sites across providers/packages) stands as-is. Drift since the audit added these 6 main.dart sites and ~3 others elsewhere; the broader re-audit can live under #3588 once this `main.dart` cleanup lands.

## Risk

Low — change is logging-only unless a step was silently throwing in production (in which case we *want* to know).

## References

- Epic: #4336
- Sibling audit: #3588
- Spec: [`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md)

title: fix(comments,share-sheet): stop silently swallowing async failures (#4336)
body:
Tracking child of epic #4336. PR C2 in the epic plan — addresses two silent-failure outliers surfaced during the round-9 BLoC audit.

## Problem

Two BLoCs combine a high catch-block count with **zero** `addError(` calls, so async failures are completely invisible:

| BLoC | catch blocks | addError sites |
|------|-------------:|---------------:|
| `mobile/lib/blocs/comments/comments_bloc.dart` | 16 | 0 |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/share_sheet/share_sheet_bloc.dart` | 10 | 0 |

`comments_bloc.dart` is the canary: every catch silently resets a loading flag, so a failure surfaces to the user as a hung-spinner-that-stops-spinning with no recovery path. `share_sheet_bloc.dart` is the same shape on share actions.

This violates both [`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md) ("avoid adding new silent-failure patterns") and the epic's [Agent Execution Notes](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4336#:~:text=avoid%20adding%20new%20silent-failure%20patterns).

## Scope

Ship **before** the Reportable classification overlay (PRs C / E / F). Two phases:

1. **Audit every catch block** in both BLoCs. For each, choose one of:
   - Add `addError(e, stackTrace)` (raw, **no Reportable wrap yet** — keeps Crashlytics quiet via the gating rule until classification PRs land).
   - Leave un-`addError`'d with a one-line comment justifying the silence (e.g., "no-op cleanup; failure has no caller-visible effect").

2. **For `comments_bloc` specifically**: every catch that resets `isLoadingMore: false` (or similar loading sentinel) must also emit a `CommentsError` status-enum value so the UI can render a real failure affordance, not a stop-spinning-but-blank state.

## Coordination

- #3715 (assigned @rabble) already targets the **classic Vine import** sliver of `share_sheet_bloc`. Either:
  - This PR closes #3715 (encompassing scope), **or**
  - This PR explicitly excludes the classic-Vine sub-path so #3715 ships independently.
  Decide with @rabble before opening the PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `grep -c 'addError(' mobile/lib/blocs/comments/comments_bloc.dart` ≥ 12 (was 0).
- [ ] `grep -c 'addError(' mobile/lib/blocs/share_sheet/share_sheet_bloc.dart` ≥ 6 (was 0).
- [ ] Every remaining silent catch carries a justifying inline comment.
- [ ] `comments_bloc` no longer leaves the UI in a "spinner-stops-but-no-error" state on any failure path; `blocTest` regressions cover at least 3 representative paths.
- [ ] PR description includes a `(site, addError-added / left-silent-with-comment, reason)` table.
- [ ] `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` + comments/share-sheet scoped tests green.

## Out of scope

- Reportable classification overlay. Comes later in PRs C / E / F. This PR only ends the *silent* failure mode.

## Risk

Low. Adding `addError(e, st)` *raw* (without Reportable) keeps Crashlytics quiet — the BlocObserver gates Crashlytics on `ReportableError`. The change surfaces failures in the unified log + `blocTest` errors clause only.

title: All reporting surfaces fail silently on TestFlight builds
body:
## Summary

All reporting surfaces (content reports, user reports, bug reports, feature requests) fail silently on TestFlight build 1.0.13+720. Tapping "Report" after selecting a reason produces no error and no confirmation — the dialog appears to do nothing.

Bug reports show "Failed to send bug report. Please try again later." — the only surface with visible error feedback.

Local builds work correctly.

## Affected surfaces

1. **User report from profile** — NIP-56 via `ContentReportingService.reportUser()`
2. **Content report from video/share menu** — NIP-56 via `ContentReportingService.reportContent()`
3. **Content report from DM conversation** — NIP-56 via `ContentReportingService.reportContent()`
4. **Bug report dialog** — Zendesk native SDK via `ZendeskSupportService.createStructuredBugReport()`
5. **Feature request dialog** — Zendesk native SDK via `ZendeskSupportService.createFeatureRequest()`

## Root cause analysis

### Issue 1: ContentReportingService initialization race

`contentReportingServiceProvider` creates a `ContentReportingService` and calls `initialize()`, which checks `_nostrService.isInitialized`. If the `NostrClient` hasn't completed relay manager initialization at that moment, the service permanently caches `_isInitialized = false`. Every subsequent `reportContent()` / `reportUser()` call returns `ReportResult.failure('Reporting service not initialized')` without retry.

The initialization order in `NostrService._onAuthStateChanged` changed recently: `state = newClient` now fires **before** `await newClient.initialize()`, exposing watchers to an uninitialized client. Previously, the state was set **after** initialization, so watchers always received an initialized client. This removed the "healing" path that previously corrected any early broken evaluations from the `build()` microtask window.

`ContentReportingService.initialize()` is not retry-safe — it checks `isInitialized` once and never re-checks. The service is cached by the Riverpod provider and never re-initialized.

### Issue 2: Error feedback invisible behind bottom sheet

The report dialog (`ReportContentDialog`) opens as a `VineBottomSheet` with `useRootNavigator: true`. Error feedback uses `ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar()`, which renders the snackbar on the scaffold **behind** the modal bottom sheet. The user sees nothing — no error, no confirmation.

This isn't new but was previously masked because reports succeeded. Now that reports fail, the invisible error feedback makes the failure appear as "nothing happens."

### Issue 3: Zendesk REST API fallback never configured on CI

`ZENDESK_API_TOKEN` has never been in `codemagic.yaml`. When the native SDK path fails, the REST API fallback checks `ZendeskConfig.isRestApiConfigured` (`apiToken.isNotEmpty`) which is always `false` on CI builds. This is by design (REST fallback is for macOS only) but means there's no safety net for native SDK failures.

## Fix plan

A PR is in progress to address:

1. **Make `ContentReportingService` initialization resilient** — re-check `_nostrService.isInitialized` at report time, not just at construction. If the client initialized after the service was created, recover gracefully.
2. **Surface errors in the report dialog** — replace `ScaffoldMessenger` snackbar with inline error state visible within the bottom sheet (matching the bug report dialog's pattern of inline result messages).
3. **Cover all reporting surfaces** — ensure the fix applies to content reports, user reports, DM reports, and the video share menu report path.

## Repro

1. Install TestFlight build 1.0.13+720
2. Navigate to any user's profile
3. Tap ⋮ → Report
4. Select "User Appears Under 16"
5. Tap "Report"
6. Observe: nothing happens (no error, no confirmation)

Also reproducible via bug report dialog (Settings → Report a Bug → fill fields → Send → "Failed to send bug report").

## Environment

- Build: 1.0.13+720 (TestFlight)
- Platform: iOS
- Local builds: working correctly

title: Keycast OAuth token expiry during background silently breaks all write operations
body:
## Summary

When the app is backgrounded long enough for the Keycast OAuth token to expire (~3 hours), all write operations fail silently on resume. `KeycastRpc._call()` throws `RpcException` on HTTP 401 but no caller catches it to attempt a token refresh and retry. The user gets no re-auth prompt -- operations just fail.

This affects every RPC-only (`divineOAuth`, no local nsec) user. With `UIBackgroundModes: fetch, remote-notification` enabled (added with push notification support in #2848), iOS keeps the app process alive during extended background periods, making this a common scenario rather than an edge case.

## Affected operations

Everything that signs a Nostr event via Keycast RPC:
- Content/user reports (NIP-56 kind 1984)
- Video uploads (NIP-98 auth for Blossom)
- Push notification registration (kind 3079)
- Event publishing (likes, reposts, comments, DMs)
- Any other `sign_event` call

## Root cause

`KeycastRpc` bakes the access token in at construction time and uses it for the lifetime of the instance. When the token expires server-side, every `_call()` throws:

```
RpcException [sign_event]: HTTP 401: {"error":"Invalid or expired token. Please log in again."}
```

The refresh infrastructure exists but isn't wired to mid-session failures:
- `OAuthClient.refreshSession()` and `getSessionOrRefresh()` can obtain fresh tokens
- `AuthService.tryRefreshExpiredSession()` can refresh and rebuild identity
- `AuthService._hasExpiredOAuthSession` tracks the expiry state
- The Settings screen shows a "Session Expired" tile when the flag is set

But:
- `_hasExpiredOAuthSession` is only set during `initialize()` and `signInForAccount()` -- never on a mid-session 401
- `AuthService.onAppResumed()` reconnects bunker signers and nostrconnect relays but does not check/refresh the OAuth token
- No caller of `KeycastRpc._call()` catches `RpcException` to attempt refresh-and-retry

## Why this wasn't visible before

Before push notification support (#2848, April 2026), the app did not declare `UIBackgroundModes`. iOS would kill the process more aggressively during extended background, leading to cold launches that run `AuthService.initialize()` -> `refreshSession()` -> fresh token. Push notifications added `UIBackgroundModes: fetch, remote-notification`, which tells iOS to keep the process alive for push delivery -- making warm resumes (with stale tokens) the common path instead of cold launches (with token refresh).

## Log evidence

From `openvine_full_logs_2026-05-20T17-33-22`:

```
[10:24:46] App launch -- signing succeeds (kind 27235, kind 3079)
[10:25:55] App enters background
[12:59:49] Delayed background suspension (process still alive after ~2.5 hours)
[13:26:54] App resumes -- first sign_event -> HTTP 401
[13:26:54+] Every subsequent sign_event fails with 401 for the rest of the session
```

The app resumed ~20 times after the first 401 failure. `onAppResumed()` ran each time. No token refresh was ever attempted.

## Suggested fix directions

**Option A: Refresh on resume** -- `AuthService.onAppResumed()` checks token expiry via `KeycastSession.isExpired` and calls `refreshSession()` before any signing attempt. Simplest, handles the common "came back from background" case.

**Option B: Retry on 401** -- Wrap `KeycastRpc._call()` (or the signing path in `NostrIdentity`) with catch-401 -> `refreshSession()` -> reconstruct `KeycastRpc` -> retry. Handles mid-foreground expiry too, but more invasive.

**Option C: Proactive refresh** -- Schedule a timer based on `KeycastSession.expiresAt` to refresh before expiry. Most robust but adds complexity.

These aren't mutually exclusive -- A is cheap and covers the main scenario, B/C are additive.

## Related

- #4586 -- Reporting surfaces failing silently (symptom of this issue for reports)
- PR #4587 -- Inline error display for reports (makes signing failures visible, doesn't fix the token expiry)
- PR #4444 -- Fix local nsec export for Keycast-backed accounts (acknowledges RPC-only account type)
- PR #4162 -- Session readiness gating (stabilized provider lifecycle, `KeycastRpc` instances live longer)
- #2848 -- Push notification support (added `UIBackgroundModes` that changed background process lifetime)

title: observability: enrich Crashlytics context for Bloc errors (event name / state snapshot / build tag)
body:
Follow-up from PR #3534's review — addresses concern #3 in @hm21's original blocker list, which was deferred from PR1 with an explicit follow-up offer.

## Current state (after PR #3534)

`DivineBlocObserver` forwards to Crashlytics:
- `error.runtimeType` (used as the dashboard grouping key)
- the stack trace
- the sanitized inner-error `toString()` (npub/nsec stripped)
- the observer's `reason` annotation: `Bloc.addError <BlocType>`
- the optional `Reportable.context` call-site tag

## Gap

When triaging a Crashlytics report, you can see *which bloc* raised, but not:
- which **event** was in flight when the error fired (handler-throw or `addError` from inside a handler)
- the **state snapshot** at the time of the error
- the **build tag** / app version (Crashlytics has this generally, but cross-referencing per-error is friction)

For race conditions like #3503 — where the symptom depends on auth-state timing — that triage gap is what made the original investigation expensive.

## Proposed surface

- Track the latest event per bloc via `BlocObserver.onEvent` (or `onTransition`) → store as a per-bloc field on the observer.
- Track the latest state per bloc via `BlocObserver.onChange` → same.
- On `onError`, set Crashlytics custom keys (`bloc.lastEvent`, `bloc.lastState`, `bloc.lastTransitionAt`) before `recordError`.
- Sanitize state snapshots through `sanitizeForCrashReport()` before they leave the device — same npub/nsec handling.
- Build tag: surface via `FirebaseCrashlytics.setCustomKey('build_tag', ...)` once at startup, not per-error.

## Out of scope

- The per-feature `addError` migration stack (PR2–PR7). That is purely the call-site classification work; this issue is a separate observability-layer change.
- Replacing the existing `Log.error` + `addError` pair convention.

## References

- PR #3534 — establishes the observer + matrix
- Discussion: https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/3534#discussion_r3169300470 (open inline thread on `Reportable.context`, where the typed-id direction was deferred for the same reasons that apply here)

body:
## Summary

**Final sub-batch (9c of 3) of #4506's split wave.** Refs #4339 Wave 2.

Moves the **15-entity social/foundation/collaborator cluster** to \`lib/providers/social_providers.dart\`. After this batch, \`app_providers.dart\` is essentially a barrel of re-exports plus a single helper function.

## What moved

**3 legacy \`Provider<X>(...)\` collaborator providers:**
- \`collaboratorResponseServiceProvider\`
- \`collaboratorInviteStateStoreProvider\`
- \`collaboratorConfirmationRepositoryProvider\`

**Action/DM orchestration:**
- \`pendingActionService\` (offline NIP-25/18/01 action queue)
- \`outgoingDmRetryService\` (auto-sweep of failed NIP-17 self-wraps from #4124)

**Analytics + view publishing:**
- \`analyticsService\` (Kind 22236 view-event publisher)

**Hashtags:**
- \`hashtagCacheService\` (persistent hashtag selection state)
- \`hashtagService\` (in-memory analyzer over video events)

**Per-user content:**
- \`draftStorageService\`
- \`clipLibraryService\`

**Identity lifecycle:**
- \`userDataCleanupService\` (sign-out / identity-change cleanup orchestrator)

**Social / NIP-51:**
- \`socialService\` (Kind 30000 follow sets)

**Content management:**
- \`contentReportingService\` (NIP-56)
- \`contentDeletionService\` (NIP-09)

**Diagnostics:**
- \`bugReportService\` (NIP-17 encrypted reports + Blossom uploads)

## Migration pattern (mirrors 9a/9b)

\`\`\`dart
// app_providers.dart
export 'social_providers.dart';  // keeps 20+ external consumers' imports unchanged
\`\`\`

social_providers.dart now imports the owning sibling provider files directly (auth_providers, relay_providers, repository_providers, upload_media_providers, video_providers), so the new file does not depend on the app_providers.dart barrel.

## Scope cleanup

- \`dart fix --apply\` removed **33 newly-unused imports** from \`app_providers.dart\` and **7** from \`social_providers.dart\` (5 unnecessary + 2 fully unused).
- **Deleted \`app_providers.g.dart\` entirely** — no \`@riverpod\` annotations remain in \`app_providers.dart\`, so the codegen file has nothing to produce. Dropped the \`part 'app_providers.g.dart';\` directive.
- Three section divider comments removed (FOUNDATIONAL SERVICES, DEPENDENT SERVICES, "(Removed duplicate legacy provider for StreamUploadService)") since their content all moved out.

Codegen moved: 15 \`*Provider\` chunks (~675 LoC) relocated from \`app_providers.g.dart\` into \`social_providers.g.dart\`.

## What's left in \`app_providers.dart\`

After this batch, the file is **40 lines**:
- Header (ABOUTME)
- 7 imports (just the helper's deps — \`flutter_riverpod\`, \`videos_repository\`, \`moderation_providers\`, \`feature_flag_providers\`, \`blocklist_content_filter\`)
- 11 \`export\` statements (the re-export barrel)
- \`createBlockedAuthorFilter\` helper function (14 lines)

The helper still has 3 callers across \`moderation_providers.dart\`, \`repository_providers.dart\`, and \`video_providers.dart\`. Moving it (alongside the rest of the back-import cleanup) is tracked under **#4554**.

| Original (audit baseline) | **2,918** | — |

title: refactor(state): define and enforce Riverpod/BLoC migration boundaries
body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
High

## Problem
Docs say BLoC/Cubit is the default for UI state, but UI paths still mix Riverpod providers, BLoC providers, service notifiers, and bridge providers without a clear ownership boundary.

## Evidence
- docs/STATE_MANAGEMENT.md:12 says BLoC/Cubit is the default for UI state.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:12 says mixed Riverpod + BLoC + service notifiers increase cognitive load.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:39 prefers BLoC/Cubit for new UI state.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:110 warns against Riverpod bridges without TODO/issue linkage.
- mobile/lib/router/app_shell.dart:37 is a ConsumerStatefulWidget while :528 reads DmUnreadCountCubit via context.watch.
- mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart:17 is a ConsumerWidget that creates a BlocProvider.
- mobile/lib/screens/apps/apps_directory_screen.dart:16 is a ConsumerWidget that creates a BlocProvider.
- mobile/lib/screens/explore_screen.dart:50 remains a large Riverpod-driven UI screen while feed-related BLoCs exist elsewhere.

## Impact
New code can accidentally extend the hybrid model instead of shrinking it. Ownership of UI state, side effects, and rebuilds remains unclear.

## Recommended fix
Define an explicit boundary: Riverpod owns app-level DI and long-lived services; BLoC/Cubit owns feature UI state and UI side effects; temporary bridges need issue links and removal criteria.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Architecture docs include concrete allowed/disallowed patterns.
- [ ] Current bridge widgets/providers are identified and linked to migration issues.
- [ ] One representative mixed screen is converted to Page/View split as a template.
- [ ] Review/lint guidance prevents new long-lived Riverpod UI providers.
- [ ] Docs reference current issue numbers and no stale migration claims.

## Related issues
Likely related: #3185, #3073, #3120, #2444, #2447.
